subject: Emotions
title: Keeping Surprise Alive
description: A 60-second lesson on Keeping Surprise Alive.

hook.text: Long-term couples report less excitement over time. Not because love fades, but because surprise does.

buildup.text: Arthur Aron's research shows that couples who try novel activities together report higher relationship quality.

discovery.text: Novelty triggers dopamine, which the brain associates with the partner. New experiences feel like new love.

twist.text: Routine isn't the enemy of love. It's the enemy of surprise. And love needs surprise to stay neurochemically alive.

climax.text: The lesson extends beyond romance: friendships, careers, and hobbies all need novelty to avoid neural adaptation.

punchline.text: Don't change your partner. Change your routine.

quiz.question: What did Arthur Aron find about novel activities in relationships?
